summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani (1920–2009) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Banaras Hindu University under A. S. Altekar, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London under K. de B. Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.

Aiko Okoshi (1946–2021) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University around 1970–1975 and served as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro (born 1956) works in Buddhist studies, having studied at Bedford College, London, and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.

Ajahn Brahm (born 1951) is a scholar and monk in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, he trained under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah (~1975–1983) and became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1984.

Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2003.

Ajahn Pasanno (born 1949) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar and monk. He studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1975 to 1982 and was founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto (born 1949) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971), became a disciple of Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, and served as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho (born 1934) is a Buddhist studies scholar and monk. He earned degrees from the University of Washington and UC Berkeley, trained under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977), and served as abbot at Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. A pupil of Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, he served as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Akifumi Naito (born 1956) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku University and Honganji Sōgakuin, he studied under Gadjin M. Nagao and held teaching posts at Ryukoku University, the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, and other institutions.

Akihiko Akamatsu (born 1953) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held academic and administrative posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, including vice-presidency (2010–2014).
Akihiro Oda works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and later as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist. She studied under supervisors and teachers Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, Kazuhiko Yoshida, and Muneo Tokunaga.

Akiko Walley specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), later holding a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, having also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.

Akio Donohashi (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1975) and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Tanabe (born 1964) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo as professor from 2015.

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. Educated at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he served there from assistant to professor (1968), and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there (1954–1975) and teaching at Waseda University (1975–1985) and ICPBS (1996).

Akira Miyaji (born 1945) works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University, he taught at Hirosaki University, became emeritus professor at Nagoya University, directed the Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and joined Ryukoku University in 2013.
